introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

The paper contains eight questions.
enonce_intro_markdown:
Three forces $\mathbf{F}_1$, $\mathbf{F}_2$ and $\mathbf{F}_3$ act through the points with position vectors $\mathbf{r}_1$, $\mathbf{r}_2$ and $\mathbf{r}_3$ respectively, where

$\mathbf{F}_1 = (3\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j} - 4\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{N}$, $\mathbf{r}_1 = (\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}$,

$\mathbf{F}_2 = (-\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{N}$, $\mathbf{r}_2 = (\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}$,

$\mathbf{F}_3 = (-\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{N}$, $\mathbf{r}_3 = (\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}$.
incertitudes: Question 1 (ii) : le sujet dit que le système des quatre forces est « en équilibre », ce qui est impossible avec les données imprimées (R.G = 4, différent de 0, voir (i) : aucune force unique ne peut annuler le moment). Le corrigé le signale et démontre la propriété qui conduit exactement au point 3k (F = -R, moment restant parallèle à F) ; l'énoncé d'origine du jury est probablement différent (sujet défectueux ou mal reproduit). Données relues à haute résolution : F1, F2, F3, r1, r2, r3 comme imprimés.
Question 1 : scan peu net ; les vecteurs ont été relus à 200 dpi.

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that this system does not reduce to a single force. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A system of forces reduces to a single force if and only if its resultant $\mathbf{R}$ is non-zero and $\mathbf{R}\cdot\mathbf{G} = 0$, where $\mathbf{G}$ is the total moment about a point (here the origin). This scalar product is the same whichever point is used, so it decides the question.

**Resultant.**

$$\mathbf{R} = \mathbf{F}_1+\mathbf{F}_2+\mathbf{F}_3 = (3-1-1)\mathbf{i}+(-2+1+0)\mathbf{j}+(-4+0+4)\mathbf{k} = \mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}\ \ \mathrm{N}$$

**Moments about the origin** ($\mathbf{M}=\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{F}$).

$$\mathbf{M}_1 = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}&\mathbf{j}&\mathbf{k}\\1&0&1\\3&-2&-4\end{vmatrix} = \mathbf{i}(0+2)-\mathbf{j}(-4-3)+\mathbf{k}(-2-0) = 2\mathbf{i}+7\mathbf{j}-2\mathbf{k}$$

$$\mathbf{M}_2 = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}&\mathbf{j}&\mathbf{k}\\0&1&1\\-1&1&0\end{vmatrix} = \mathbf{i}(0-1)-\mathbf{j}(0+1)+\mathbf{k}(0+1) = -\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k}$$

$$\mathbf{M}_3 = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}&\mathbf{j}&\mathbf{k}\\1&1&1\\-1&0&4\end{vmatrix} = \mathbf{i}(4-0)-\mathbf{j}(4+1)+\mathbf{k}(0+1) = 4\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k}$$

$$\mathbf{G} = \mathbf{M}_1+\mathbf{M}_2+\mathbf{M}_3 = 5\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+0\mathbf{k}\ \ \mathrm{N\,m}$$

**Test.**

$$\mathbf{R}\cdot\mathbf{G} = (1)(5)+(-1)(1)+(0)(0) = 4 \neq 0$$

Since $\mathbf{R}\neq\mathbf{0}$ but $\mathbf{R}\cdot\mathbf{G}\neq 0$, the moment of the system has a component along $\mathbf{R}$ that no single force through any point can produce. Hence the system does **not** reduce to a single force (it reduces to a force $\mathbf{R}$ together with a couple, that is, a wrench).

questions.enonce_markdown: When a fourth force $\mathbf{F}$ is added, the system of four forces is in equilibrium. Show that $\mathbf{F}$ acts through the point with position vector $(3\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}$. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**The force $\mathbf{F}$.** For the four forces to have no resultant, $\mathbf{F}=-\mathbf{R}=-\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}$ N.

**A remark on the wording.** Taken literally, "equilibrium" is impossible here: by part (i), $\mathbf{R}\cdot\mathbf{G}=4\neq0$, and a single added force $\mathbf{F}=-\mathbf{R}$ has a moment $\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{F}$ perpendicular to $\mathbf{F}$, so it can never cancel the component of $\mathbf{G}$ along $\mathbf{R}$. What the added force can do is remove the resultant and leave a system whose moment is parallel to $\mathbf{F}$ itself. This condition fixes the line of action and gives exactly the point $3\mathbf{k}$ asked for, so it is the one used below.

**Condition.** Let $\mathbf{F}$ act through the point with position vector $\mathbf{r}$. The four forces then have zero resultant, so their moment is the same about every point:

$$\mathbf{G}_{\text{total}} = \mathbf{G}+\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{F}.$$

Split $\mathbf{G}$ into a part parallel to $\mathbf{F}$ and a part perpendicular to it. With $\mathbf{F}=-\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}$ and $|\mathbf{F}|^2=2$:

$$\mathbf{G}_{\parallel}=\frac{\mathbf{G}\cdot\mathbf{F}}{|\mathbf{F}|^2}\mathbf{F}=\frac{-5+1}{2}(-\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}) = 2\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j},\qquad \mathbf{G}_{\perp}=\mathbf{G}-\mathbf{G}_{\parallel}=3\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}.$$

Since $\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{F}$ is always perpendicular to $\mathbf{F}$, the total moment is parallel to $\mathbf{F}$ exactly when

$$\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{F} = -\mathbf{G}_{\perp} = -3\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}.$$

**Check for the point $3\mathbf{k}$.**

$$3\mathbf{k}\times(-\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}) = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}&\mathbf{j}&\mathbf{k}\\0&0&3\\-1&1&0\end{vmatrix} = \mathbf{i}(0-3)-\mathbf{j}(0+3)+\mathbf{k}(0) = -3\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}\ \checkmark$$

So $\mathbf{F}=-\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}$ N acts along the line through the point $3\mathbf{k}$ m (any point of the line $\mathbf{r}=3\mathbf{k}+\lambda(-\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})$ gives the same moment). The remaining moment of the whole system is $\mathbf{G}_{\parallel}=2\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}=-2\mathbf{F}$ N m, a couple parallel to $\mathbf{F}$.
